newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bldg consents up 12.7 pct in October year.
newsitem.headline: NZ bldg consents up 12.7 pct in October year.

text.p: The total value of building consents for the October year was $6.12 billion, up 12.7 percent on the October 1995 year, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.
For non-residential buildings, consents with a total value of NZ$2.53 billion were authorised in the year ended October, a rise of 20.8 percent from the year ended October 1995.
SNZ said consents for non-residential buildings were continuing the steady growth which began in early 1996.

In the month of October, the value of non-residential consents was NZ$229.4 million, including $59.3 million for hotels and motels, $42.8 million for factories and industrial buildings, and $32.5 million for shops, restaurants and taverns.
In contrast, SNZ said, the trend for residential buildings has been declining since May, although provisional figures for November indicate the decline in the trend had levelled off.
The value of consents for residential buildings in October was NZ$310.1 million. Consents for 1,875 new dwelling units were issued in October.
The national median consent value for new dwelling units authorised in October was $120,000, a rise of 9.1 percent on the year-ago figure.
